title: Design a Notification Service
relevance: High — staple LLD / machine-coding + bridge-to-HLD question (campus + experienced); Uber, Microsoft, Amazon, Flipkart, Meta, LinkedIn, Airbnb-style loops probe multi-channel Strategy/Adapter, Observer decoupling, preferences, retries, and concurrency.
company_notes: Campus/new-grad machine-coding or LLD in India (Amazon, Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, Microsoft-style) expects a working multi-channel demo plus pattern names; SDE-2/experienced probes Adapter failover, retries/DLQ, idempotency, rate limits, async boundaries, and priority vs promo isolation; FAANG/product OOD often starts as LLD then expands toward HLD (queues, APNs/FCM, preferences DB). Among the most asked design-a-service LLD problems after parking lot / rate-limiter utilities.

phases.goal: Lock mandatory multi-channel FR/NFR, preference and status behavior, and in-scope extensions before designing classes.

must_hit.point: Mandatory FR: send via at least Email, SMS, and Push; create a notification from an event/request; respect user channel preferences; track basic success/fail status.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate lists Email/SMS/Push, event-driven create, preference gating, and status tracking as non-negotiable.

must_hit.point: NFR: new channels without rewriting the orchestrator (OCP), no tight coupling to vendor SDKs, correctness under concurrent sends; optional async queue for scale talk.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions extensibility, vendor decoupling, concurrent correctness, and may note async enqueue as a stretch NFR.

must_hit.point: Common extensions to ask: templates, priorities (HIGH/MED/LOW), retries + fallback, rate limits / quiet hours, scheduled send, digests, in-app inbox, delivery webhooks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Proactively asks which extensions are in scope rather than coding all of them.

must_hit.point: State assumptions: in-memory prefs/templates OK for machine coding; third-party APIs mocked; at-least-once OK unless exactly-once is required.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly states in-memory mocks and at-least-once delivery assumption.

probes: What must we support on day one versus what is an extension we should clarify first?
Walk an Order placed, OTP, Push-fails-fallback-SMS, and promo-opt-out scenario against your FR list.

hints.1: Start by naming channels and whether preferences apply to every event type.
hints.2: Split mandatory FR (multi-channel send, prefs, status) from extensions (templates, retries, quiet hours, digests).
hints.3: Say: Email/SMS/Push mandatory; OTP ignores promo opt-out; Push fail may fall back to SMS; in-memory prefs and mocked providers for machine coding.

phases.goal: Name the core nouns and their responsibilities so routing, prefs, and channels are separable.

must_hit.point: Core entities include Notification/NotificationRequest (id, userId, type, priority, payload/context, status), Channel, NotificationTemplate with render, and UserPreferences (opt-in per type×channel, quiet hours, caps).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists notification request fields, template render, and preference dimensions without dumping everything into one god object.

must_hit.point: NotificationChannel/ChannelHandler is the Strategy send leaf; optional NotificationProvider Adapter wraps Twilio/SendGrid/FCM; NotificationService is the Facade/orchestrator.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates channel strategy, optional vendor adapter, and service facade roles.

must_hit.point: Optional supporting types: RetryPolicy, RateLimiter, queue/NotificationTask for async dispatch and reliability.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names retry/rate-limit/queue task types as optional collaborators, not mandatory for every scope.

probes: What objects appear if we start from a food-delivery OrderPlaced story?
Where do templates and preferences live relative to the channel that actually sends?

hints.1: List nouns from the story: notification, channel, template, preference, retry.
hints.2: Keep NotificationRequest/status separate from Channel Strategy and Template.render.
hints.3: Sketch Notification + Template + UserPreferences + NotificationChannel + NotificationService (+ optional Provider/RetryPolicy).

phases.goal: Wire Facade, Strategy/Factory, optional Adapter/Observer/Decorator so producers and vendors stay decoupled.

must_hit.point: Dual decoupling: producers (Order/Payment) must not import Email/SMS SDKs (Observer/event bus/Pub-Sub); orchestrator must not hardcode Twilio/SendGrid (Strategy + optional Adapter behind send).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains both producer fan-out decoupling and vendor/channel send decoupling.

must_hit.point: NotificationService uses UserPreferences, TemplateRegistry, ChannelFactory/Map of NotificationChannel, and optional RateLimiter/RetryPolicy/Queue; Email/SMS/Push/InApp implement NotificationChannel.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws Facade depending on prefs, templates, factory/map, and channel strategies—not a switch forest in the service.

must_hit.point: Patterns that earn points: Strategy, Factory, Adapter, Observer, Decorator (timestamp/encrypt/retry), Facade, Command (queueable send), optional Singleton manager (prefer DI in production).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names Strategy/Factory/Facade at minimum and can place Adapter/Observer/Decorator/Command where they fit.

must_hit.point: SOLID signal: OCP for new channel/provider/event without editing orchestrator; SRP across template/channel/preference/service; DIP on NotificationChannel/NotificationProvider abstractions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties class boundaries to OCP/SRP/DIP rather than only naming patterns.

probes: Why must Checkout not import Email/SMS/Push directly?
Where does Factory sit relative to NotificationChannel and optional vendor Adapters?

hints.1: Avoid a god notify() that scatters send calls and hardcodes vendors.
hints.2: Facade orchestrates; Strategy per channel; Factory resolves channel; Observer for event fan-out.
hints.3: OrderService publishes; NotificationService observes; ChannelFactory.get returns Email/SMS/Push strategies that may call Adapters.

phases.goal: Show the routing pipeline and method surface: prefs → channels → render → rate-limit → dispatch → status.

must_hit.point: Routing is the hard path: event → load preferences → pick channels → render template → rate-limit → dispatch; sending is the easy leaf.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Narrates preference-gated channel selection and template render before any channel.send.

must_hit.point: API surface includes notify(userId, eventType, context) or notify(NotificationRequest), setPreferences, registerTemplate, getStatus; OOD methods: isAllowed, Template.render, Channel.send, ChannelFactory.get, RetryPolicy.shouldRetry/nextDelay.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches Facade notify plus prefs/template/channel/factory/retry method signatures.

must_hit.point: Templates store subject/body with placeholders; Template.render(context) keeps copy out of if (type == ORDER_PLACED) god methods.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows placeholder templates rendered with context instead of hardcoded bodies in the service.

must_hit.point: Preferences & compliance: opt-out promotional; never opt-out security/OTP (or force Email+SMS); quiet hours skip Push/SMS but allow CRITICAL; frequency caps per channel.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gates by type×channel and explains OTP/CRITICAL overrides vs promo quiet-hours/caps.

probes: Walk notify for Order placed → Email receipt + Push through your classes.
How do quiet hours and OTP/CRITICAL interact with UserPreferences.isAllowed?

hints.1: Sending is easy; preference and template routing is the design.
hints.2: Service: validate → prefs/rate limits → render → per-channel dispatch → record status.
hints.3: Call isAllowed, render template, ChannelFactory.get(channel).send, then update status; OTP bypasses promo opt-out.

phases.goal: Show how new channels, fallbacks, digests, and async scale talk extend the design without rewriting the Facade.

must_hit.point: Add WhatsApp without changing NotificationService by adding WhatsAppChannel and Factory registration (OCP); fail if you switch inside the service.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Registers a new strategy in the factory/map and leaves the Facade untouched.

must_hit.point: Push failed → try SMS via fallback chain / Chain of Responsibility or explicit FallbackPolicy—not buried inside one channel class.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Places fallback policy outside a single channel implementation.

must_hit.point: Strategy-only vs Strategy+Adapter: Strategy enough for mocks; Adapter lets you swap Twilio without touching channel policy (failover providers).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains when a vendor Adapter layer is worth adding for provider failover.

must_hit.point: Digest example: buffer low-priority events then flush on timer (batching vs real-time); async stretch enqueues NotificationTask with per-channel workers and retry/DLQ outside the request thread.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes digest buffering and optionally queue/workers/DLQ without building Kafka unless asked.

probes: Add WhatsApp without editing NotificationService—what changes?
If Push fails, where does fallback SMS live in the object model?

hints.1: New channel should be a new class, not a new case in the service.
hints.2: Factory registration + optional FallbackPolicy/CoR for channel failover.
hints.3: WhatsAppChannel + factory entry; FallbackPolicy maps Push→SMS; digests buffer then flush; narrate Kafka workers/DLQ in minutes if asked.

phases.goal: Keep preference reads and dispatches safe, avoid double-send, and prevent Observer notify/unsubscribe deadlocks.

must_hit.point: Concurrency needs: thread-safe preference reads; concurrent dispatches across users; don’t double-send the same notificationId (idempotency key).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions safe pref reads, parallel per-user dispatch care, and idempotency on notificationId.

must_hit.point: Two workers on the same message: idempotency key + status CAS (PENDING→SENT); gotcha of naive at-least-once.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses CAS/status transition so retries do not spam (e.g. OTP twice).

must_hit.point: Pub-sub notify must not mutate the subscriber list unsafely—copy-on-write / concurrent structures; calling Observer notify while holding a lock while a subscriber unsubscribes can deadlock—copy the listener list first.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Copies listeners before notify and avoids holding the subscription lock across subscriber callbacks.

must_hit.point: Fan-out: parallelize channel sends per user carefully; never share mutable notification status without sync; isolate slow SMS from email workers with per-channel limiters.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Synchronizes status updates and isolates channel workers/rate limiters under load.

probes: Two workers pick up the same notification—how do you avoid sending OTP twice?
What goes wrong if you notify observers while holding the subscriber-list lock?

hints.1: Think idempotency and shared status, not only more threads.
hints.2: Idempotency key + PENDING→SENT CAS; copy listener list before Observer notify.
hints.3: At-least-once workers claim via CAS on notificationId; never notify under lock while unsubscribe can run.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Strategy alone is enough for mocked multi-channel sends in machine coding; adding Adapter around Twilio/SendGrid/FCM shows provider failover and swapping vendors without changing channel policy.
Sync send is demable in a timed machine-coding round; for scale/retries say you’d enqueue NotificationTask and use per-channel workers/DLQ—don’t build Kafka unless asked.
In-process Observer is same-JVM and simple for LLD; Pub-Sub/queue is durable and multi-service—name both and pick based on interview scope.
Low-priority social events can buffer and flush on a timer for digests; critical/OTP paths stay real-time and must not sit behind promo blasts (priority vs surge isolation).
At-least-once workers need notificationId/idempotency key and status CAS so retries don’t double-send OTP; exactly-once is out of scope unless asked.

gotchas.trap: God-class NotificationService with hardcoded bodies and vendor HTTP calls.
gotchas.correction: Split Template.render, Channel Strategy send, optional Provider Adapter, and Facade orchestration.

gotchas.trap: Adding WhatsApp by switching inside NotificationService.
gotchas.correction: New WhatsAppChannel plus Factory registration (OCP)—do not edit the Facade’s channel switch.

gotchas.trap: Burying Push→SMS fallback inside one channel class.
gotchas.correction: Use an explicit FallbackPolicy or Chain of Responsibility outside a single channel.

gotchas.trap: Honoring promo opt-out for OTP/security notifications.
gotchas.correction: Gate by notification type; security/OTP overrides preferences (force Email+SMS as needed).
CRITICAL bypasses quiet hours/rate limits; promo does not.

gotchas.trap: Naive at-least-once: two workers process the same message and spam.
Calling Observer notify while holding a lock as a subscriber unsubscribes.
gotchas.correction: Copy the listener list first (or use concurrent/copy-on-write structures) so notify cannot deadlock with unsubscribe.
